headline: Record production + Hess synergies lift earnings
summary_short: Chevron delivered record Q2 2026 earnings of $12.1B ($6.11 diluted EPS) on 20% y/y production growth from legacy Hess assets and record US refinery throughput. Achieved $1.5B of Hess synergies ahead of schedule and paid down $8.4B in debt.
summary_long: Reported earnings of $12.07B were 5× Q1's $2.21B, reflecting record US production, record refinery utilization (97%), and $1.4B in favorable timing. Upstream contributed $8.18B (+200% y/y) on Hess assets and Permian/Gulf growth. Downstream at $4.87B benefited from stronger refined-product margins. Cash flow from operations $22.6B (vs $2.5B in Q1); FCF $18.1B. Debt reduced by a record $8.4B. Hess synergies of $1.5B captured within one year (50% ahead of target). Structural cost target hit six months early with $3B run-rate savings. Signed 20-year Microsoft power deal for West Texas data center.

drivers.explanation: Record US upstream production (contribution from legacy Hess assets + Permian/Gulf of America growth), record US refinery crude throughput at 97% utilization, higher commodity prices, and $1.4B in favorable timing effects.
Record US production combined with higher commodity prices, increased cash distributions from Tengizchevroil LLP, and favorable working capital effects.
Legacy Hess assets contribution + growth in the Permian Basin and Gulf of America drove Q2 production to 4,070 MBOED (+20% y/y).

confidence_notes: Filing-based summary from Exhibit 99.1 of the July 31 2026 8-K. All KPI values quoted directly from the press release. Q/Q deltas computed vs Q1 2026 data (also disclosed in the same table). Adjusted earnings and FCF are non-GAAP measures reconciled in Attachment 4 of the release.
